semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "Generative flow network" is a specific type of generative model, indicating that it falls directly under the category of generative modeling. It is semantically equivalent in terms of being a subset of generative modeling, even though it specifies a particular approach.

Similar to "generative flow network," the plural form "generative flow networks" represents the same type of deep learning model used for generative purposes. Therefore, it is considered semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: All generative models, including the Given Model, are a type of neural network model. Neural network models serve as an umbrella category, making it the parent model.

closest_parent_model.justification: Since all generative models derive from neural network models, and there are no broader categories listed, "neural network models" is the closest and one of the only suitable parents provided.

child_models.justification: These models are a specific approach within the broader category of generative modeling, making them child models.

closest_child_model.justification: VAEs are perhaps the most fundamental specific instantiation of generative models in this list, commonly used as a baseline in generative modeling techniques.

sibling_models.justification: A model focused on adversarial training methods while focusing on the generation of new data, similarly to the focus of the Given Model.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Given that "generative modeling" covers a wide array of modeling techniques focused on data generation, GANs are a closely related method sharing this primary focus.
